grades.quote: sleep releases the pipe’s lock as part of putting pipewrite’s process to sleep.
grades.reason: Shows the correct xv6 sleep/wakeup pattern (condition protected by a lock, sleep releases the lock, sleeping in a loop), which is background for avoiding a lost wakeup. It doesn't describe the failure or diagnose why a thread sleeps forever.

grades.quote: Along with the condition lock, it helps prevent wakeup from overlooking a process that is calling sleep but has not finished yielding the CPU.
grades.reason: States that p->lock together with the condition lock keeps wakeup from overlooking a process that is calling sleep but hasn't finished yielding. That is the lost-wakeup mechanism behind the symptom. It is only one bullet in a broader list, so it is a partial answer.

grades.quote: When a waiting thread releases the mutex in order to wait on the condition variable, these two actions are done indivisibly. There is no way another thread can acquire the mutex before the first thread has started waiting on the condition variable. This ensures no other thread will do a notify operation until after the thread that wants to wait is actually waiting.
grades.reason: Explains the mechanism behind lost-wakeup sleeps. Releasing the mutex and starting to wait happen indivisibly, so no notify can slip in before the thread is waiting. It also says the wait must be in a loop that rechecks the condition. It doesn't directly walk through diagnosing a thread stuck after a notify.

grades.quote: waiting for a condition variable should always be done using a loop, because when the thread finishes waiting, it may not be the first to acquire the mutex. For example, a thread that is notified because data was placed into a bounded buffer may find that another thread has meanwhile emptied the buffer back out.
grades.reason: Only auxiliary information. It says condition waits must be in a loop because another thread may change the state before the woken thread reacquires the mutex, and because of spurious wakeups. That bears on wakeup and condition mismatches, but it doesn't address a thread sleeping forever after the condition changed and a wakeup already ran. The rest of the passage is bibliographic history.
